definitions.explanation: A craftsperson who builds and repairs wooden structures and objects, especially houses and buildings.

examples.japanese: {大工|だいく}に{家|いえ}の{修理|しゅうり}を{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I asked a carpenter to repair the house.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{腕|うで}のいい{大工|だいく}だった。
examples.english: My grandfather was a skilled carpenter.
examples.notes: 腕のいい = skilled, good at one's craft

examples.japanese: {大工|だいく}{仕事|しごと}は{体力|たいりょく}が{必要|ひつよう}だ。
{父|ちち}は{日曜|にちよう}{大工|だいく}で{棚|たな}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: My father built a shelf as a DIY project.
examples.notes: 日曜大工 = Sunday carpenter, DIY

examples.japanese: {宮|みや}{大工|だいく}は{釘|くぎ}を{使|つか}わずに{神社|じんじゃ}や{寺|てら}を{建|た}てる{技術|ぎじゅつ}を{持|も}っている。
examples.english: Shrine carpenters have the technique of building shrines and temples without using nails.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE: Traditional Japanese {大工|だいく} (carpenters) are highly skilled craftsmen. The construction of traditional Japanese wooden buildings, including temples and shrines, requires specialized techniques passed down through generations.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {町|まち}{大工|だいく} (town carpenter)
- {宮|みや}{大工|だいく} (shrine/temple carpenter - specialized)
- {大工|だいく}{道具|どうぐ} (carpentry tools)
- {日曜|にちよう}{大工|だいく} (Sunday carpenter, DIY enthusiast)

IDIOM: {大工|だいく}の{掘|ほ}っ{立|た}て{小屋|ごや} = 'The cobbler's children have no shoes' (lit. 'a carpenter's hastily-built shack')
